Papa Zaka's Spiced Rum Offering

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Approximately 1 quart (1 liter)Prep 10 min (plus 24-48 hours infusion)

This spiced rum offering is a traditional way to honor Papa Zaka, the Lwa of agriculture and farmers, during the Fete de Papa Zaka. It's a simple, heartfelt preparation, symbolizing the bounty of the earth and the spirit's connection to the land.

Ingredients

  • 1 (750 ml) bottle white rum (or clairin, if available)
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) brown sugar
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 3-4 whole cloves
  • 1/2 teaspoon whole allspice berries
  • 1 small piece (1 inch / 2.5 cm) fresh ginger, sliced
  • 1/2 vanilla bean, split (optional)

Method

  1. In a clean, airtight glass bottle or jar, combine the white rum, brown sugar, cinnamon stick, whole cloves, allspice berries, sliced ginger, and optional vanilla bean.
  2. Seal the bottle or jar tightly.
  3. Shake gently to help dissolve the brown sugar.
  4. Store in a cool, dark place for at least 24 to 48 hours, shaking occasionally, to allow the flavors to meld and infuse.
  5. Before serving or offering, you may strain out the spices if desired, or leave them in for continued infusion and visual appeal.
  6. Serve neat in small glasses as an offering, or dilute with a splash of water or coconut water if preferred for drinking.

Tips

  • For a more authentic offering, use clairin, a traditional Haitian white rum, if accessible.
  • Adjust the amount of spices to your preference; you can add a pinch of nutmeg or a strip of orange peel for extra complexity.
  • This spiced rum can also be used as a base for simple cocktails, mixed with fresh fruit juices like pineapple or orange.
